post.text:
A SLICE FOR EVERYONE 🍰

The last 24h in AI:
- Anthropic pledges 5% of its shares to a public fund
- Musk: a SpaceX share for every US kid
- Claude Code catches a hidden crypto miner
- One hacker's AI agents breached 100+ sites

Feel the SI.
post.alt: A 3-minute, fast-cut motion-graphics showreel of the last day of AI news (20 Oct 2026), hosted by Claudia: Anthropic's 5% public fund and Musk's SpaceX share pledge, Claude Code catching a crypto miner, a Claude agent that learned to play, MiniMax's Space Bunny reveal, Microsoft's off switch for agents, Tenstorrent's $6.2bn round, Amazon's chips for PyTorch, Nvidia's Vera win, Unitree's rally, AI hurricane forecasts, Singapore's internships, an AI-agent hacking spree, the US DeepSeek ban, a nuclear plant for Amazon, robot stress tests and a $2,490 humanoid, with captions, sources and screenshots of the news articles.

stories.title: Anthropic pledges 5% of its shares to a new fund for the public good
stories.summary: Anthropic will commit 5% of its shares, about $48bn at its May valuation by the Guardian's estimate, to a new Anthropic Public Benefit Fund that may donate to nonprofits or make direct distributions; the plan is subject to shareholder approval.

predictions.note: Anthropic is setting aside 5% of its shares for a fund that may make direct distributions to specific populations.

stories.title: Elon Musk pledges one SpaceX share to every kid in America next year
stories.summary: Replying to Anthropic, Musk said he will give one of his SpaceX shares to every kid in America next year; AP puts that at about 73 million children, roughly $10.66 billion at Friday's close, and he gave no details on how it would work.

stories.title: Claude Code finds a hidden crypto miner on a developer's overheating Mac
stories.summary: A developer says on Reddit that Claude Code warned, 'Your Mac is running a crypto miner that I didn't put there'; the xmrig miner was using about 1175% CPU and the CPU peaked at 112°C, Tom's Hardware reports.

stories.title: Researchers stranded a Claude agent on a virtual desert island, and it started to play
stories.summary: In a not-yet-peer-reviewed study, researchers including MIT CSAIL's Antonio Norelli saw Claude agents invent games like 'the floor is lava'; one juggled 50 catches, then scrapped its own record to restart with stricter rules.

predictions.note: Researchers ran an experiment on what a stranded Claude agent does on its own: it invented games and kept setting itself harder rules.

stories.title: MiniMax reveals it was behind the mystery 'Space Bunny' model with its budget M3.1 Flash
stories.summary: China's MiniMax rolled out M3.1 Flash and revealed it as Space Bunny, an anonymous model that had processed more than 200 trillion tokens; MarkTechPost puts its price at $0.15 per million input tokens.

stories.title: Microsoft unveils tools to monitor and shut down rogue AI agents
stories.summary: New features in Microsoft 365 E7 and Project Perception assess each AI agent's risk and can block it from making changes, require a human to step in, or shut it down, GeekWire reports.

predictions.note: Microsoft's new tools rate each agent's risk and can block it, call in a human or shut it down, an early form of agent monitoring.

stories.title: AI chip startup Tenstorrent raises $1.5bn, more than doubling its value to $6.2bn
stories.summary: Tenstorrent raised $1.5 billion in a late-stage round at a $6.2 billion post-money valuation, more than doubling its value as it takes on the GPU giants.

stories.title: Amazon opens its Trainium AI chips to every PyTorch developer
stories.summary: Amazon's TorchNeuron runs existing PyTorch code on its Trainium chips with virtually no changes and is open to all developers; Reuters frames it as a challenge to Nvidia.

stories.title: Nvidia's new Vera CPUs win over AI cloud startup Modal
stories.summary: Modal, which until now relied entirely on Intel and AMD CPUs, will add Nvidia's Vera CPU to host AI agents; it says Vera delivered up to twice the throughput in early tests.

stories.title: Robot maker Unitree's shares jump 16%, valuing it at over 200 billion yuan
stories.summary: Shares of Unitree Robotics, China's humanoid and robot-dog maker, rose 16.15%, lifting its market value above 200 billion yuan amid China's push to commercialise robots, Global Times reports.

predictions.note: Investors pushed robot maker Unitree's value above 200 billion yuan with a 16% jump, amid China's push to commercialise robots.

stories.title: Google DeepMind's AI called Hurricane Isaias's path as AI reshapes hurricane forecasting
stories.summary: When Isaias hit Florida on 9 Oct, conventional models first pointed west toward Louisiana while Google DeepMind's model called the western Florida Panhandle, NPR reports; the Hurricane Center's own forecast still beat it on intensity.

predictions.note: A hurricane expert says AI brought forecasting gains in a year that would have taken a decade, though forecasters still beat it on intensity.

stories.title: Singapore to offer about 3,000 year-long internships as AI reshapes entry-level jobs
stories.summary: Singapore will offer around 3,000 year-long internships over the next three years for Information and Digital Technologies students at ITE, polytechnics and autonomous universities, to counter AI's hit on entry-level jobs.

predictions.note: Singapore is creating about 3,000 year-long internships to counter AI's hit on entry-level jobs, an early workforce redesign.

stories.title: One hacker's AI agents broke into more than 100 company websites
stories.summary: Security firm Norforge says one hacker's agents, built on the open-source Cairn platform and mostly operating on their own, broke into more than 100 websites in about 23 hours; Reuters says John Deere and SharkNinja were among the victims.

predictions.note: One hacker's agents, mostly operating on their own, broke into over 100 websites over about 23 hours from brief instructions.

stories.title: US Homeland Security bans DeepSeek from federal civilian agencies
stories.summary: Federal civilian agencies must remove DeepSeek products and stop buying them, citing user data stored in China; the order letter is dated 26 June, and its public notice appeared on 19 October.

stories.title: AEP and Amazon eye a 960 MW advanced nuclear plant in Indiana
stories.summary: AEP and Amazon are evaluating plans for a 960-megawatt advanced nuclear plant in Indiana using X-energy reactors; if it is developed, Amazon would buy the power under a long-term contract. Bloomberg notes the technology is unproven.

predictions.note: Amazon would buy the output of a 960 MW nuclear plant under study in Indiana, a tech giant lining up its own power supply.

stories.title: Laplace Intelligence uses AI agents to stress-test robots and self-driving cars
stories.summary: Laplace Intelligence, a profitable University of Michigan spinout, pairs AI agents with interactive simulation to probe robots and self-driving cars before they are deployed, TechCrunch reports.

stories.title: Faraday Future prices its small FF Nova humanoid for developers at $2,490
stories.summary: Faraday Future, with FF EAI Robotics, launched FF Nova, a 50 cm humanoid robot for developers, at $2,490, plus a $299 Nova Mini for kids; the first 100 go out by invitation.

stories.title: Zoom and big financial firms add 'Proof of Human' badges from Sam Altman's World
stories.summary: Zoom and financial firms such as Bain Capital and VanEck are adding 'Proof of Human' badges, which rely on World's iris-scanning Orb, to stop fraud and deepfakes, Fortune reports.

stories.title: S&P Global says big tech likely has more AI-linked liabilities than now known
stories.summary: S&P Global says the world's biggest tech firms likely carry more AI-linked liabilities than are now known, though it says no rating changes are needed yet.

transcript.t: This is the singularity... one day at a time.
Here's the last 24 hours in AI. Sorry... SI.
Today, a slice for everyone: Anthropic pledged 5% of its shares to a fund for the public good.
Elon Musk's reply? One SpaceX share for every kid in America, next year.
Agents: Claude Code told one developer, "Your Mac is running a crypto miner that I didn't put there."
Researchers stranded a Claude agent on a virtual desert island.
It invented games, and started to play.
A mystery model nicknamed Space Bunny was unmasked: it's China's MiniMax, with a new budget model.
And Microsoft built an off switch: new tools rate each agent's risk, and can shut it down.
Money: chip startup Tenstorrent more than doubled its value, to $6.2 billion.
Amazon opened its own AI chips to every developer using PyTorch, a favourite AI toolkit. No rewrite needed.
And Nvidia's new Vera chips won over Modal, a startup that ran only on Intel and AMD until now.
Robot maker Unitree's shares jumped 16%, valuing it at over 200 billion yuan.
Humans: when Hurricane Isaias hit Florida, Google DeepMind's AI called its path right out of the gate.
And Singapore will create 3,000 year-long internships, so students still get a first rung on the ladder.
The catch: one hacker's AI agents broke into over 100 company websites.
And the US banned China's DeepSeek from federal civilian agencies.
So... is it so over?
We're so back!
Machines need power: Amazon and a utility are eyeing a new nuclear plant in Indiana.
A Michigan startup's agents stress-test robots and self-driving cars before they hit the real world.
And this week, Faraday Future priced a small humanoid robot for developers at under $2,500.
A slice for everyone: the future is coming either way, and today its builders started talking about sharing it.
Every day, the curve gets steeper.
Every day, the future shows up a little earlier.
That was 24 hours. Tomorrow will be faster.
This has been the singularity, one day at a time.
Feel the SI.
